title: CAMEL: Co-Designing AI Models and eDRAMs for Efficient On-Device Learning
problem: Training deep neural networks on resource-limited edge devices demands substantial memory and frequent data access, while eDRAM's periodic refresh cycles consume significant power and can degrade overall system performance.
motivation: On-device learning enables AI models to quickly adapt to local user data, improving service quality and latency on edge platforms.
method: The approach leverages eDRAM as the primary on-chip memory for transient training data, exploiting its higher density and lower leakage power compared to SRAM. Reversible DNN architectures are co-designed to minimize data lifetime during training, thereby reducing refresh operations. The CAMEL training engine coordinates eDRAM memory with optimized dataflow to lower memory footprint and off-chip DRAM traffic.
key_novelty: Co-designing reversible DNN architectures with eDRAM-based storage to minimize data lifetime and eliminate expensive refresh operations during on-device training.
contributions: Reversible DNN architectures that reduce data lifetime and storage costs during training
CAMEL on-device training engine optimized for eDRAM as primary on-chip memory
Achieves 2.5× speedup and 2.8× energy savings versus baseline hardware platforms
primary_theme: eDRAM-optimized on-device DNN training with hardware-algorithm co-design
